# A small assortment of factoring methods, covering the seven families that
# build_cofactoring_strategies splits its input into: PM1, PP1-27, PP1-65,
# and ECM with each of BRENT12, MONTY12, MONTY16 and MONTYTWED12. Three
# methods per family: the zero method, then B1/B2 = 100/1000 and 150/3000.
#
# test_missing_method_family.sh reads it, removes one family at a time, and
# checks that build_cofactoring_strategies diagnoses the gap instead of
# indexing into an empty family.
#
# The numbers are made up, not measured. The first family carries plausible
# values, and each later family repeats them with 0.01 less probability
# (floored at 0.01) and one microsecond more time, so that the seven are
# distinguishable and ordered. Nothing here says anything about how these
# methods really perform; the test only needs families that parse.
#
# One consequence of that ordering is worth knowing: since each family is
# strictly worse than the one before it, only the first few ever survive
# the trade-off frontier, so the strategies pinned under expected/ name
# PM1, PP1-27, ECM-B12 and ECM-M12 and nothing else. What covers the
# remaining families is test_missing_method_family.sh, which removes each
# of them in turn.
#
